text.p: September notionnel futures traded on MATIF will be confined to a tight range between 130.34 and 130.74 on Monday in the absence of any clearcut signals from technical indicators, analysts said.
Brenda Sullivan, technical anlayst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, said in the very short term, the contract had set channel support at 130.40, followed by a more convincing prop at 130.34.
"If we break lower through that channel support at 130.40 to retest 130.34, there's a strong risk of a break lower to continue towards retracement near 130.06," said Sullivan.
"That'll cause a lot more problems on the daily charts."
Charts show the market hit a daily low of 130.34 on Friday. By 0750 GMT, September notionnel futures on MATIF were down 12 basis points at 130.48.

"The short term range has clear levels, but we don't know which way it will get broken yet," said Sullivan. "I rather suspect it will be the downside, but it's risky to say that at the moment because we don't have good strong technical evidence to say one way or the other."
Sullivan said that to the upside, the contract may test 130.58/68 ahead of the 130.70 retracement level.
"Upward gains might extend through 130.74 but they would be limited to 130.90 for the immediate term," she added.
David Wood, independent technical analyst near London, said the contract's main barrier on Friday was at 130.66/80, adding if it could pierce that, then 130.90 was on the cards.
"But the market is more likely to consolidate for a while, then go lower towards 130.00," said Wood. "The main long-term swing support is at 129.80, the low on July 15."
Wood said the market would have to close below this level in the longer term to confirm the bearish tone.
By 0805 GMT, September Pibor was down 0.01 at 96.49.
